$comment: PF-446 — golden signature vectors. GENERATED ONCE and committed. Regenerating is a deliberate act with a diff, never a silent refresh: these are what stop the server signer and the SDK verifier from drifting into agreeing only with themselves. See signatureVectors.test.ts.
scheme: HMAC-SHA256 over utf8(`${timestamp}.`) || utf8(rawBody), rendered as `t=<seconds>,v1=<lowercase hex>`

vectors.name: ordinary-envelope
vectors.note: The shape a real document.created carries. The base case.

vectors.name: empty-body
vectors.note: A zero-length payload is not an error case. A verifier that special-cases empty input diverges here.

vectors.name: non-ascii
vectors.note: Multi-byte UTF-8, an em dash and an astral-plane emoji. A verifier that hashes over a JS string rather than bytes gets a different digest here.

vectors.name: delimiters-in-body
vectors.note: The body contains the header's OWN delimiters, including a decoy t=/v1= pair. A verifier that split the body on ',' or scanned it for the signature breaks here.

vectors.name: forward-slash
vectors.note: JSON.stringify does not escape `/`, but many serializers do. This pins that the bytes are taken as-is.

vectors.name: second-secret-same-body
vectors.note: Identical bytes to ordinary-envelope under a DIFFERENT secret. The two headers must differ — that is the fanout property the matcher relies on.

vectors.name: epoch-zero
vectors.note: Timestamp 0. Number("") is also 0, so a parser using Number() instead of a digit check would accept an EMPTY t and land here.

vectors.name: large-timestamp
vectors.note: Year 2100. Guards against a 32-bit truncation in any reimplementation.
